dependencies.reason: uses the request pipeline's authentication position, public routes, the error envelope and the list helper
uses the loaded configuration ([[oauth.providers]], external_url), the store with transactions and migration, and the stored admin-token hash and admin_email

tasks.title: Authenticate the admin token, API keys and PATs on every non-public route
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/authenticate_test.go and internal/identity/credential_test.go, with a test hub helper in internal/identity/testhub_test.go that builds the request pipeline of internal/server over a store in t.TempDir() and registers the test routes whoami and me, and confirm they fail; packages 05 and 06 extend this helper and do not write a second one

Create the identity tables through the schema migration of internal/store: users (id, username unique, email unique, full_name, role, status, provider and provider_id unique as a pair, created_at, updated_at), orgs (id, name unique, slug unique, url, owner_id nullable, status, created_at, updated_at), memberships (org_id and user_id unique as a pair, created_at), API keys (key_id, user_id, secret hash, expires_days, expires_at nullable, revoked_at nullable, created_at) and PATs (token_id, user_id, secret hash, name, permissions, paths nullable, workspace nullable, expires_at nullable, revoked_at nullable, created_at)

Generate credentials from crypto/rand in the three wire formats: an API key as parley_<8>_<32> over [0-9A-Za-z], a PAT as parley_pat_<8>_<32> over [a-z0-9]; store the lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of the secret part and never the secret; return the full value once to the caller

Add the store functions later packages and the tests use: create a user, issue an API key for a user with a lifetime in days, store a PAT for a user with name, permissions, paths, workspace and expiry inside a transaction it is given, generating the id again when it exists (the store-level write that package 06's minting operation wraps; no other production code calls it), and look a key or PAT up by its id

Recognise a credential by exact format (admin: parley_admin_ plus 64 characters of [0-9a-f]); read it from the Authorization header with the scheme Bearer matched without regard to case, one or more spaces between scheme and credential, surrounding white space ignored

Answer 401 unauthenticated with the message "authentication required" for a missing header, another scheme, an empty credential or an unknown format, and 401 with "invalid credentials" for an unknown id or a secret that does not match; compare hashes with crypto/subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, and run the comparison against a fixed dummy hash when the id is unknown so both cases take the same path

Verify an admin-format token through the verification function of internal/identity/admin.go that package 03 created; answer "invalid credentials" when it does not match or the hub is not bootstrapped

Report the caller to the pipeline: type (admin, api_key, pat), credential id (admin, key_id or token_id), the user with role and status or none, and a PAT's permissions, paths and workspace; expose the same credential check as a function that takes the credential string, so the git server of package 17 can call it with a Basic password

Add the route declaration "needs a user" as a named mark of package 02's route registration, read by the authenticator right after it accepted the credential, which answers the admin token 403 forbidden with the message "this route needs a user"

Install the authenticator in the authentication position of package 02's pipeline and register this package's schema step on the composition of package 03, in internal/hub/identity.go, so every non-public route under /api/v1 is authenticated

tasks.title: Refuse revoked and expired credentials and the credentials of blocked users
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/authenticate_test.go and confirm they fail; add the admin-token flow to test/e2e/auth_test.go
Give the authenticator its clock as a parameter, the system clock in production

After the secret matched, and only then, check in this order: revoked_at set is 401 "credential revoked"; the current time at or after expires_at is 401 "credential expired" (null never expires); a user whose status is blocked is 403 forbidden "user is blocked"
Keep a wrong secret answered "invalid credentials" with the same body whatever the state of the credential or its user
Read the credential and its user's status from the store on every request, so that a revocation, a block and an unblock take effect on the next request and blocking changes no credential record

tasks.title: List the configured identity providers
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/providers_test.go and confirm they fail

Describe the two supported providers, github and google, with their default authorize, token and user URLs and their scopes (user:email; openid email profile), and resolve each configured [[oauth.providers]] entry against them, taking authorize_url, token_url and userinfo_url from the entry when set
Build authorize_url as the authorize endpoint with the query parameters client_id and scope, plus response_type=code for google

Register the public route GET /auth/providers: answer the configured providers ordered by name through the list helper of internal/server, each as {name, authorize_url}, with Cache-Control: public, max-age=300; an empty configuration answers an empty items array
Never copy client_secret into the answer
Register the route on the hub's composition in internal/hub/identity.go, from the loaded configuration

tasks.title: Exchange an OAuth code and read the user's identity from the provider
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/oauth_test.go, against a fake provider built on httptest that records its requests, and confirm they fail

Add the provider client with one operation that takes a provider name, a code and a redirect_uri and returns an identity {provider, provider_id, username, full_name, email} or an error of the kind rejected or upstream; the HTTP client and the timeout (15 seconds by default) are parameters
Exchange the code with one form-encoded POST to the token URL carrying client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri and grant_type=authorization_code and the header Accept: application/json

Treat a JSON answer with an error member and a status below 500 as rejected, and every other answer without an access token (network error, status of 500 or above, a body that is not a JSON object, no access_token) as upstream

Read the GitHub identity from the user URL with Authorization: Bearer: id as a decimal string, login, name, email; when email is null or empty read the user URL with /emails appended and take the entry with primary and verified both true
Read the Google identity from the user URL: sub, name as username and full name, email only when email_verified is true
Trim the username; when it is empty use <provider>-<provider_id>
Return upstream when the user URL or the e-mail list does not answer 200 with the expected JSON, or when the id or the verified e-mail is missing
Bound each call by the timeout and close the connection when it passes; build error texts from fixed words only, never from the code, the client secret, the access token or the provider's body

tasks.title: Create the user, the personal org and an API key at a first login
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/login_test.go and internal/identity/slug_test.go and confirm they fail; the handler takes the provider client as an interface so the tests can set the identity it returns, and its clock as a parameter

Register the public route POST /auth/callback, not a create route (so Idempotency-Key is ignored): decode the body {provider, code, redirect_uri, expires}, read the identity through the provider client, and run the sign-in

Sign-in, in one store transaction: look the user up by provider and provider_id; when none exists create the user with status active, the username and e-mail of the identity and the provider's display name as full_name
When the username is another user's, try <name>-2 to <name>-10 in order; when none is free fail with a conflict
Set the role to admin when the e-mail equals the stored bootstrap admin_email ignoring letter case and no user with role admin exists in any status; otherwise user

Derive the personal org's slug from the final username: lowercase, replace characters outside [a-z0-9_-] with -, collapse runs of -, trim leading and trailing - and _; fewer than 2 characters left gives u-<first 8 characters of the user id>; a leading digit gets the prefix u-; a taken slug tries <slug>-1 to <slug>-10 in order

Create the org with name equal to the username, owner_id the user and status active, and the membership of the user, in the same transaction; export this creation as one function that takes an open transaction, the user's fields and the role and returns a conflict error when the username, the e-mail or the provider identity is taken, an org has the username as its name, or no slug is free; the sign-in picks the username suffix and the role before calling it, and package 05 calls it from POST /users with role user

Issue an API key for the user with the requested lifetime (expires_at is the login time plus expires x 24 hours, null for 0, 90 days when absent) and answer 200 {user, api_key: {key, key_id, expires_at}} with timestamps written through internal/server/timefmt of package 02
Answer 409 conflict and roll the whole transaction back when the e-mail belongs to another user, an org already has the username as its name, or no free username or slug is found

tasks.title: Refresh an existing user at login and replace the user's API keys
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/login_test.go and confirm they fail
When the identity matches a user by provider and provider_id and the user is blocked, answer 403 forbidden with the message "user is blocked" and change nothing
Otherwise refresh email and username from the identity and set updated_at; keep id, role, full_name, created_at and the personal org untouched
When the new username belongs to another user, keep the old username and go on; when the new e-mail belongs to another user, answer 409 conflict and roll back

In the same transaction, for a new and for an existing user alike, set revoked_at on every API key of the user that is neither revoked nor expired, then issue the new key; leave already revoked keys, the user's PATs and other users' keys untouched

tasks.title: Validate the login callback and report provider failures
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/identity/login_test.go and internal/identity/providers_test.go, running the real provider client against the fake provider, and confirm they fail

Validate the body before any call to the provider: provider, code and redirect_uri are required strings, code is non-empty, provider names a configured provider, expires is absent, null or one of the integers 0, 30, 60 and 90; a violation is 400 invalid_request

Validate redirect_uri: parse it as an absolute URL; allow scheme http with host localhost or 127.0.0.1 and any port and path; allow a URL whose scheme, host and port (with the scheme's default port filled in) equal those of [server].external_url when that is set; refuse everything else, including URLs with user information, with 400 invalid_request

Map the provider client's errors: rejected is 401 unauthenticated; upstream, including a timeout and an identity without id or verified e-mail, is 502 upstream_error; both with fixed messages that contain no code, secret, token or provider body
Make sure every refusal leaves the store unchanged: no user, org, membership or key created and no key revoked
Wire the production provider client, with its 15-second timeout and the configured providers and external_url, into the callback route registered in internal/hub/identity.go
Confirm both public routes answer the same with no Authorization header and with one that would fail authentication

tasks.title: Store a credential with parley login --api-key and save the client configuration file
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/cli/login_test.go and internal/cli/config_test.go, against a stub hub built on httptest, and confirm they fail
Use github.com/BurntSushi/toml, which package 03 added to go.mod; add no second TOML module

Create internal/cli/config.go, the file package 09 later extends into the one read and save of every command, and locate the config file: $PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR/config.toml when the variable is set and non-empty, otherwise .parley/config.toml under the user's home directory
Read the file into a map; a missing file is an empty map; a file that is not valid TOML fails parley login before any request with exit status 2 and a client_error envelope

Save: set endpoint_url (without trailing slashes), api_key and user_id in the map, keep every other key, create the directory with mode 0700 when missing, write a temporary file with mode 0600 in the same directory and rename it over config.toml; on failure remove the temporary file and report client_error with a message that says the credential was accepted and not saved

Add the command parley login to the root command with the flags --provider (default github), --expires (default 90) and --api-key; resolve the hub URL from --endpoint-url, PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL and the file key endpoint_url, in that order; with none, fail with exit status 2 and a client_error that names all three

Key flow, chosen by the flag --api-key alone: take the credential from the flag, or from stdin when the value is -, trimmed; an empty credential is a usage_error; send GET <hub>/api/v1/user with Authorization: Bearer and a 30-second timeout
On 200 save the file, print the User on stdout as one JSON document indented by 2 spaces with a trailing newline, and print "Logged in as <username>" on stderr; exit 0

On a hub error print the envelope on stderr exactly as received and exit 1; on a connection failure or an answer that is not a JSON object print an envelope with code 0 and error_type client_error and exit 2; in both cases print nothing on stdout and save nothing

Give the login command the error type it needs for this (exit status plus envelope) in internal/cli/login.go; package 09 replaces it with its shared error types and exit-code mapping and moves login onto its client

tasks.title: Sign in through the browser with parley login
steps: Add the task's behaviours to internal/cli/login_test.go, with a browser opener and a wait the test supplies, and confirm they fail; add the first-login and second-login flows to test/e2e/login_test.go with a fake GitHub
Validate --expires (0, 30, 60 or 90) before any request; another value is a usage_error with exit status 2

Fetch GET <hub>/api/v1/auth/providers without a credential and pick the item whose name equals --provider; a hub error is printed as received with exit status 1; an unreachable hub, an unreadable answer or a provider that is not listed is a client_error with exit status 2, the last naming the providers the hub lists

Listen on 127.0.0.1 port 0; build the URL to open by adding redirect_uri=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback and a state of 32 hexadecimal characters from crypto/rand to the provider's authorize_url as query parameters, keeping the parameters it has

Open the URL with the opener (open on macOS, xdg-open on Linux, rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler on Windows; a parameter of the command's constructor); when it fails print the URL on stderr and keep waiting

Serve GET /callback once: a code together with the state that was sent answers 200 with a short HTML success page; another state, an error parameter or a missing code answers 400 with a short HTML failure page and fails the login with client_error, exit status 2; compare the state in constant time
Wait at most 120 seconds (a parameter of the constructor) for the redirect; on expiry fail with client_error, exit status 2; close the listener on every way out
Send POST <hub>/api/v1/auth/callback with {provider, code, redirect_uri, expires} and no Authorization header; a hub error is printed as received with exit status 1

On 200 save endpoint_url, api_key.key and user.id through the config file code, print the user object alone on stdout, indented by 2 spaces, and "Logged in as <username>" on stderr; never print the key
done_when: `go test ./test/e2e/... -run Login -count=1` passes against an in-process hub and a fake GitHub
